stem: A planner wants to detect a 10% relative lift on a 4% baseline conversion and puts δ = 0.10 into Lehr's rule, n per variant ≈ 16 × p(1 - p) / δ². What goes wrong?

options.text: Nothing: Lehr's rule takes the relative lift as δ, so 0.10 is the right value
δ must be the absolute difference, 0.004, so 0.10 gives a sample far too small
δ = 0.10 gives a sample far too large, so the test would run for far too long
δ must be the baseline itself, 0.04, so 0.10 is too large a value for the rule
